title: Stepwise velocity throttles and tenant lease decay (PRD - idea)
content:
Context
This doc sketches a mechanism for controlling short-term tenant bursts and longer-term capacity fairness using two coupled levers: stepwise velocity throttles (a short-window SLA-aware throttle) and tenant lease decay (a medium-term soft reservation expiration). Target: reduce noisy-neighbor tail latency, make bursts predictable, and give tenants transparent signals and credit for aggressive short bursts without hard preemption.

Why this? (problem statement)
- Dedicated pools currently allow bursty patterns to cause latency spikes for other tenants in the same pool.
- Existing burst credit designs are all-or-nothing or require heavy manual ops to tune.
- We want a system that: (1) protects latency SLOs at the pool level, (2) provides predictable short burstability for tenants, (3) gracefully reduces burst privileges over time if sustained high velocity is observed, and (4) is operationally simple to debug.

Goals (measurable)
- Maintain 99th-percentile token latency within SLO (e.g., 250ms) for tenants flagged as "low-latency" during normal and burst periods 95% of the time.
- Reduce noisy-neighbor incidents (defined as >2x baseline tail latency spikes attributed to other tenant load) by 60% over baseline in pilot pools.
- Keep average tenant rejection rate for bursts below 3% while enforcing pool-level latency guarantees.
- Expose clear billing/usage signals so customers understand burst consumption.

Non-goals
- This doc doesn't attempt to replace reservation or billing models; it's a runtime traffic shaping layer.
- Not addressing inter-region routing or multi-pool tenant fencing in this iteration.

High-level approach
1) Stepwise velocity throttles (SVT) - short window, low-latency protective throttle
   - Measure tenant request velocity in short epochs (e.g., 15s sliding window + 60s smoothing).
   - Maintain per-tenant velocity bands (e.g., baseline, boosted, excessive). Each band maps to a soft concurrency/throughput throttle and a per-token latency budget.
   - SVT acts as a fast-acting governor that reduces new request acceptance or shifts priority to lower-fidelity lanes (e.g., best-effort) when tenant velocity crosses thresholds.
   - Velocity thresholds are model-aware (larger seq length models have lower thresholds), and configurable per-tenant tier.

2) Tenant lease decay (TLD) - medium-term lease that decays if tenant sustains high velocity
   - When a tenant exceeds baseline velocity but remains within boosted window, they consume from a "lease" token that has a measured capacity (credits).
   - Lease tokens have a time-decayed credit balance (exponential or linear decay) to reclaim burst headroom automatically after heavy usage stops.
   - If tenant keeps consuming at high velocity and depletes lease credits, SVT steps in with stronger throttles or degraded lanes.
   - Admins can optionally configure tenancy-level lease sizes (paid boost vs included boost).

3) Isolation guardrails and soft-fallbacks
   - Pool-level latency monitors feed a controller that can enforce global dampening (across tenants) when pool tail latencies degrade.
   - Provide automatic fallbacks: model variant downgrade, reduced max tokens, or route to dedicated-preemptible lanes.
   - Soft-eviction only as last resort: move requests to queued mode rather than immediate rejection. Clear telemetry emitted when queued.

Design details / signals
- Observability: emit per-tenant velocity histogram, lease-balance, throttle-state-change events, and pool-latency-heatmaps.
- Telemetry naming: ded.svt.velocity, ded.svt.band, ded.tld.balance, ded.pool.latency.p99.
- Config primitives: epoch_size_seconds, smoothing_half_life, band_thresholds, initial_lease_credits, decay_rate, max_boost_multiplier.
- Enforcement points: edge admission (fast path), runtime router (queue/priority), executor (model-fidelity fallback).

Operator UX and customer UX
- Console: new "Burst & Throttle" tab under Dedicated pool -> shows current lease balances, velocity spikes timeline, and per-tenant throttle status.
- API: expose endpoints for tenants to query their remaining lease credits and current velocity band.
- Notifications: proactive email/console warning when a tenant hits >75% of lease or when pool enters dampening mode.

Billing/Contracts considerations
- Default leases included with reserved capacity (e.g., X credits/month). Extra leases can be purchased or burst billing applied at usage time.
- Show estimated cost impact when tenants enable larger initial_lease_credits in the console.

Rollout plan (phased)
- Phase 0: simulation and offline replay (1 month) - run SVT and TLD on historical traffic in simulator, produce risk report. (Owners: ML infra + Eng reliability)
- Phase 1: pilot on 2 low-risk dedicated pools (2–4 weeks) - opt-in tenants, monitor p99 and lease dynamics. Add telemetry & alerting.
- Phase 2: opt-in self-serve (1–2 months) - expose UI controls, limited cohorts. Tighten thresholds based on pilot.
- Phase 3: on-by-default with conservative defaults + escalation path (3 months)

Open questions / risks
- How to choose decay function that balances aggressive reclamation vs confusing customer behavior? linear vs exponential?
- How do we attribute latency spikes accurately to a tenant vs model artifacts? Need improved traceback (trace IDs passed end-to-end).
- Do we allow cross-tenant credit transfers or shared leases for org-level pooling? (complicates billing)
- Interaction with Dedicated warm-pools / prewarm logic - risk of double-counting headroom.

Operational runbook notes (quick)
- Alert: ded.pool.latency.p99 > 2x target for > 5m -> run "dedicated-dampening" playbook: reduce max_boost_multiplier across tenants, enable queueing.
- Debug: use ded.svt.velocity spike traces to identify top contributors; check ded.tld.balance to see which tenants depleted leases.
- Customer comms: when a tenant is queued for >30s escalate to CS with recommended SLA options.

Next steps (actionable)
- Get eng feedback on enforcement points (edge vs router vs executor) - assigned to David Chen (due 2024-08-20).
- Build a simple offline simulator that replays 30 days of Dedicated production traces with configurable SVT/TLD params - Marco Ricci (due 2024-09-06).
- Design console mockups for lease visibility and alerts - Lina Alvarez + product design (due 2024-08-30).

Notes to self / TODOs
- Add detailed math section for decay curves and credit accounting (placeholder).
- Find example tenants with spiky daily patterns for pilot recruitment.
- Align billing language with Finance (Priya).

Quick sketch of config example (human-readable)
- epoch_size_seconds: 15
- smoothing_half_life_seconds: 60
- band_thresholds: { baseline: 10 rps, boosted: 50 rps, excessive: 200 rps }  // model-adjusted in practice
- initial_lease_credits: 300 (equiv to ~10m tokens)
- decay_rate: 0.5 per hour (exponential)

If this direction looks promising we should convert into a formal PRD with concrete SLAs for pilot tenants and a simulation results appendix.

-- Asha
